import sys
input = sys.stdin.read
data = input().split()

def min_extra_tiles_needed(tiles):
    # Parse the tiles
    parsed_tiles = [(int(tile[0]), tile[1]) for tile in tiles]

    # Check for a mentsu (koutsu or shuntsu)
    def is_koutsu(t1, t2, t3):
        return t1 == t2 == t3

    def is_shuntsu(t1, t2, t3):
        numbers = sorted([t1[0], t2[0], t3[0]])
        return t1[1] == t2[1] == t3[1] and numbers[2] - numbers[1] == 1 and numbers[1] - numbers[0] == 1
    
    # Check if there is already a mentsu
    n = len(parsed_tiles)
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            for k in range(j + 1, n):
                if is_koutsu(parsed_tiles[i], parsed_tiles[j], parsed_tiles[k]) or is_shuntsu(parsed_tiles[i], parsed_tiles[j], parsed_tiles[k]):
                    return 0

    # Check if one more tile can form a mentsu
    required_tiles = set()
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            t1, t2 = parsed_tiles[i], parsed_tiles[j]
            if t1[1] == t2[1]:  # Same suit, check for potential shuntsu
                numbers = sorted([t1[0], t2[0]])
                if numbers[1] - numbers[0] == 1:  # Missing one tile to complete a shuntsu
                    required_tiles.add((numbers[0] - 1, t1[1]))
                    required_tiles.add((numbers[1] + 1, t1[1]))
                elif numbers[1] - numbers[0] == 2:  # Missing middle tile
                    required_tiles.add((numbers[0] + 1, t1[1]))
            if t1[0] == t2[0]:  # Same number, check for potential koutsu
                required_tiles.add((t1[0], t1[1]))

    # Check if one of the required tiles is already in the hand
    for t in required_tiles:
        for existing_tile in parsed_tiles:
            if existing_tile == t:
                return 1

    # If we need two more tiles
    return 2

print(min_extra_tiles_needed(data))

    # Check for a mentsu (koutsu or shuntsu)
    def is_koutsu(t1, t2, t3):
        return t1 == t2 == t3

    def is_shuntsu(t1, t2, t3):
        numbers = sorted([t1[0], t2[0], t3[0]])
        return t1[1] == t2[1] == t3[1] and numbers[2] - numbers[1] == 1 and numbers[1] - numbers[0] == 1
    
    # Check if there is already a mentsu
    n = len(parsed_tiles)
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            for k in range(j + 1, n):
                if is_koutsu(parsed_tiles[i], parsed_tiles[j], parsed_tiles[k]) or is_shuntsu(parsed_tiles[i], parsed_tiles[j], parsed_tiles[k]):
                    return 0

    # Check if one more tile can form a mentsu
    required_tiles = set()
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            t1, t2 = parsed_tiles[i], parsed_tiles[j]
            if t1[1] == t2[1]:  # Same suit, check for potential shuntsu
                numbers = sorted([t1[0], t2[0]])

                    required_tiles.add((numbers[0] - 1, t1[1]))

            if t1[0] == t2[0]:  # Same number, check for potential koutsu
                required_tiles.add((t1[0], t1[1]))

    for t in required_tiles:
        for existing_tile in parsed_tiles:
            if existing_tile == t:
                return 1

    # If we need two more tiles
    return 2

print(min_extra_tiles_needed(data))

    # Check for a mentsu (koutsu or shuntsu)
    def is_koutsu(t1, t2, t3):
        return t1 == t2 == t3

        numbers = sorted([t1[0], t2[0], t3[0]])
        return t1[1] == t2[1] == t3[1] and numbers[2] - numbers[1] == 1 and numbers[1] - numbers[0] == 1

    required_tiles = set()

                if numbers[1] - numbers[0] == 1:  # Missing one tile to complete a shuntsu

            if t1[0] == t2[0]:  # Same number, check for potential koutsu
                required_tiles.add((t1[0], t1[1]))

    for t in required_tiles:
        for existing_tile in parsed_tiles:
            if existing_tile == t:
                return 1

    # If we need two more tiles
    return 2

print(min_extra_tiles_needed(data))
